title: Two Anchors for This Mission

breakdown.detail: Know what assets you have, what risks you face, and what your current controls are. NIST CSF Function 1.
Implement the safeguards needed to limit the impact of a security event. NIST CSF Function 2.
Identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event — logging, monitoring, anomaly detection. NIST CSF Function 3.
Take action after a detected event — contain, eradicate, communicate. NIST CSF Function 4.
Restore systems and capabilities. Learn from the incident. Improve. NIST CSF Function 5.

additionalNote: NIST CSF describes a security PROGRAMME — the continuous organisational effort to manage risk. It maps onto the incident lifecycle: before an attack (Identify + Protect), during (Detect + Respond), and after (Recover). Pentesters contribute primarily to Identify and Detect — their reports tell the organisation what they missed.

secondaryAnchor.title: CVE / CWE / NVD — Remember the Hierarchy
secondaryAnchor.content:
CVE = specific case (this exact vulnerability in this exact software version)
CWE = weakness category (the class of problem — SQL injection, SSRF, etc.)
NVD = enriched database (adds CVSS score, patch info, exploit availability to CVE data)

Memory cue: CWE is the *disease type* (diabetes). CVE is the *patient case* (Patient 12345 has diabetes). NVD is the *medical journal entry* that documents severity, treatment, and prognosis.
